brief.topic: A Gentle Push and the Price of a Larger Force

s01: A small piston moves down, and a wider one rises.
Imagine an ideal liquid that does not compress.
Both chambers have the same depth into the page.
The wider piston has three times the area.
Watch the space swept out on each side.
The narrow piston moves three times as far.
Cut its colored region into three equal pieces.
Placed side by side, they fill the other region exactly.
These regions count displaced volume, not traveling parcels of water.
The same pressure change acts across both pistons.
Across three times the area, it produces three times the force.
But the larger force acts through one third of the distance.
We are ignoring friction and pressure differences from height.
Another gentle push repeats the same exchange: more force, less distance.

scenes.narration:
A small piston moves down, and a wider one rises. The liquid links their movements.

Imagine an ideal liquid that does not compress. Both chambers have the same depth into the page. The wider piston has three times the area.

Watch the space swept out on each side. The narrow piston moves three times as far. Cut its colored region into three equal pieces. Placed side by side, they fill the other region exactly.

These regions count displaced volume, not traveling parcels of water. The same pressure change acts across both pistons. Across three times the area, it produces three times the force.

But the larger force acts through one third of the distance. The ideal work is unchanged. We are ignoring friction and pressure differences from height. Another gentle push repeats the same exchange: more force, less distance.
